bloques.titulo: Modal in Konjunktiv II of the past
texto: It is formed with **hätte** + infinitive of the modal + the infinitive of the main verb: **Ich hätte früher anrufen müssen** (should have called before). The order sounds weird at first, because the two infinitives go at the end: **hätte … anrufen müssen**.
With «können» or «wollen» it does the same: **Er hätte kommen können** (could have come), **Sie hätte es wissen wollen** (would have wanted to know).
If the main verb is of movement, **wäre** (sein): **Wir wären gern gekommen** (we would have liked to come) is used. This form is used in what would have been necessary and did not happen.
Eye with the false friend: **müssen** in Konjunktiv II past is «There should be.», not «I had to».

opciones.explicacion: hätte + infinitive + müssen at the end of past Konjunktiv II.
With manners rules the double infinitive (Ersatzinfinitiv), never the gemusst participle.
Structure not in German for past obligation.

bloques.pregunta: What does «hätte … können» mean in an unreal past?

opciones.explicacion: hätte ħkönnen expresses unreal capacity or possibility in the past.
It corresponds to the actual present «kann».
It corresponds to the «konnte» Indicative Präteritum.
hätte ħkönnen indicates an unmaterialized past possibility.
It is present as an indication: Er kann kommen.
It's a real sign past: Er konnte kommen.
hätte + infinitive + müssen forms the past Konjunktiv II with verbs not of movement.
it has formed the Perfekt of indication, not Konjunktiv unreal.
wäre is reserved for intransitive verbs of movement or change of state.

opciones.texto: I would have wanted to know.
opciones.explicacion: hätte + infinitive + wollen expresses hypothetical will in the past.

opciones.texto: He wants to know right now.
opciones.explicacion: I would express the present as an indication: Sie will es wissen.

opciones.texto: He wanted to know it yesterday formally.
opciones.explicacion: It would express Präteritum: Sie wollte es wissen.

bloques.traduccion: We would have liked to come.

bloques.pregunta: What auxiliary corresponds to a verb of movement in the unreal past?

opciones.explicacion: With displacement verbs such as kommen or fahren the auxiliary sein is used in Konjunktiv II.
hätte is combined with transient verbs and most unmoved manners.
würde forma la perifrosis de present, not el paso irreal con particicio.

opciones.texto: Sujeto + hätte + adverbio + infinitivo pleno + infinitivo modal
opciones.explicacion: At the end of the main clause the two infinitive is accumulated: anrufen müssen.
Wrong order that violates the required double infinitive.
anrufen is not a verb of intransitive movement, so it does not carry sein.
